subdivision_of_building: Please note that the proposal primarily relates to the rear ground commercial unit, formerly the 'sorting office'.  However, the proposal also includes changes to the roof (new rooflights) and side elevations (new windows) of the Sorting Office and the removal of the stall on the Church Street entrance.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:DRAWING NO: 352.24/001DRAWING NO: 352.24/ 002DRAWING NO: 352.24/003DRAWING NO: 352.24/ 010BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 011BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 012DRAWING NO: 352.24/ 013BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 014BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 015BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 020BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 021BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 022BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 023DRAWING NO: 352.24/ 024BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 025BDRAWING NO: 352.24/ 030ADRAWING NO: 352.24/ 031APlanning StatementHeritage Impact Assessment Design & Access Statement Letter of Support from Enfield Post Office Post Master Transport Statement  Highway Safety Impact Pro FormaEnergy & Sustainability Statement Flood Risk Assessment and Suds Report 11.05.2026 Commercial Agency Report Daylight and Sunlight Assessment April 2026Energy & Sustainability Statement Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Form Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

No development shall take place until a Construction Management Plan (CMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Construction of the permitted development must be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan. The CMP shall include, but not be limited to, arrangements for the following in respect of each phase of the works:Site Access and Logistics:   - Details of any temporary construction access to the site, including measures for removal following completion of construction works.   - Anticipated vehicle numbers, types, and frequencies.   - Access and routing of vehicles during construction.   - Measures to manage the delivery of materials and plant to the site, including the routes and timings of deliveries and provision of loading/unloading areas.Site Management:   - Parking areas for contractors' vehicles.   - Areas for storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development, clear of the highway.   - Erection and maintenance of security hoarding.Environmental Safeguards:   - Wheel washing facilities on site to ensure that mud and debris are not spread onto the adjacent public highway.   - Other means to mitigate the impact on the public highway.   - Measures to minimise dust, noise, and vibration.Construction Operations:   - A detailed method statement and programme for the building works.   - Hours of work.   - Details of public engagement.Contact Information:   - Contact details for the responsible person (site manager/office) who can be contacted in the event of any issue.The approved CMP shall be adhered to and implemented throughout the construction period, in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure that the construction of the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or the safety of the highway, and to safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers and the local environment, in accordance with relevant policies of the Development Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework.

Prior to occupation of residential units hereby approved, details of means of enclosure for the front garden serving Flat A, including a 1.2m brick wall together with an appropriate boundary treatment between the adjacent  amenity spaces of Flat B and Flat C in the courtyard created have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The enclosure shall be provided in accordance with the approved details before the development is occupied. [GW1.1]Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance, to enhance the character of the area and to safeguard the amenities of the occupiers, in accordance with the Development Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework.

Prior to occupation of development, a landscaping scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall include, but not be limited to, the following measures:No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until a landscaping scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall include, but not be limited to, the following measures:a. Schedules of plants and trees, to include native and wildlife friendly species in appropriate locations (noting species, planting sizes and proposed numbers / densities) to be planted; b. Soft plantings: including grass and turf areas, shrub and herbaceous areas; c. Enclosures: including types, dimensions and treatments of walls, fences, screen walls, barriers, rails, retaining walls and hedges; d. Hard landscaping: including ground surfaces, kerbs, edges, ridge and flexible pavings, unit paving, furniture, steps and if applicable synthetic surfaces; and any other landscaping features forming part of the scheme. All landscaping in accordance with the approved scheme shall be completed/planted during the first planting season following practical completion of the development hereby approved. The landscaping and tree planting shall set out a plan for the continued management and maintenance of the site and any planting which dies, becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of completion of the development shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details or an approved alternative and to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details so approved and shall be maintained as such thereafter.The construction process shall be carried out only in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance, to enhance the character of the area, to provide biodiversity and ecological benefits, and to safeguard the amenities of the occupiers, in accordance with the Development Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework.

Building Recordingi) No demolition or conversion can commence until a programme of historic building recording has been secured and undertaken in accordance with a written scheme of investigation which has been submitted by the applicant, and approved by the planning authority.ii) The applicant will submit to the local planning authority an approved historic building report (to be submitted within six months of the completion of fieldwork, unless otherwise agreed in advance with the Planning Authority in consultation with the Greater London Archaeology Advice Service). This report shall be submitted to the Greater London Historic Environment Record and Local Studies Library in accordance with their guidelines and best practice.Reason: To ensure that a record is made of the building of historic interest.

Schedule of Repair and Restoration Prior to occupation of development, a schedule of Repair and Restoration shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This shall include details for the: o Cleaning of exterior brick and stone work (all elevations); o Repair of cowls; o Repair, redecoration and reinstatement of the gates, piers and railings Development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be completed in full prior to first occupation. Reason: To secure heritage benefit

Prior to the commencement of the development, evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ to allow continuing details of Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant of net power between 37kW and 560 kW to be uploaded during the construction phase of the development shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. 2. Evidence that all plant and machinery to be used during the demolition and construction phases of the development shall meets Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/ EC for both NOx and PM emissions shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. 3. During the course of the demolitions, site preparation and construction phases, an inventory and emissions records for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and detail proof of emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by Local Authority officers at all times until the completion of the development. Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health

Prior to occupation of development, the 'Shop' as identified on drawing "No.352.24/101 Existing Ground Floor Plan" shall be demolished in accordance with the approved plans with all building material removed from site. Reason: To secure heritage benefit

Notwithstanding the approved drawings, prior to insertion, revised drawings showing solid timber external doors to the 'Communal Lobby' shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

Details Prior to the insertion of windows, doors and rooflights, additional drawings by section and elevation at a scales of between 1:20 and 1:1 as appropriate shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These shall show details of proposed new: i) Windows (including stone cills, stone lintels, reveals and ironmongery) ii) Doors (including stone lintels reveals and ironmongery) iii) Rooflights Works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The windows shall be in timber, slim-profile double glazed (max 14mm) with spacer bars to match the external joinery colour, and all glazing shall be externally face puttied.The windows shall be installed and thereafter retained as such and shall not incorporate trickle vents, surface-mounted or applied glazing bars, or visible gaskets at any time. The windows shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Bin and Cyle Stores Prior to their erection, additional drawings of the bin and bike stores by section and elevation at scales of between 1:20 and 1:1 as appropriate shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such. Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

The development shall be completed in accordance with the Energy & Sustainability Statement prepared by Ecolytik dated December 2025 unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation. Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The residential development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until detailed plans showing the location and extent of air source heat pumps to be installed on the building shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. The measures shall include the installation of a meter to monitor the energy output from the approved renewable energy systems. The heat pumps shall be installed in full accordance with the details approved by the Local Planning Authority and permanently retained and maintained thereafter. Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and to safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The residential units hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Building Regulations Optional requirement G2 for water consumption of no more than 105 litres or less per head per day (excluding allowance of up to five litres for external water consumption) has been complied with. The measures shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Policy SI 5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

Prior to occupation of the residential units hereby approved,  a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved drainage / SuDS/Flood Risk measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:o	As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information o	Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systems and flood resilient and resistant measureso	Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage featureso	A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similarREASON : To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 59-62, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF

Prior to occupation, details of the cleaning, repair and refurbishment of the Church Street façade, including stonework, decorative features (including the pediment and shield), and any external finishes, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To secure heritage benefit

Rainwater GoodsAll new rainwater goods shall be of cast metal to match the profiles, thickness and decoration of the original gutters, downpipes and hoppers. Rainwater goods shall thereafter be permanently maintained as such. Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

ServicesNo electricity, internet, gas or water meter boxes shall be fixed to the external fabric of the building. All service intakes - including but not limited to electrical, water, telephone and internet - to dwellings shall be run internally and not visible on the exterior. Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Appurtenances No soil ventilation pipes, air extraction pipes, boiler flues or ducting shall be fixed to the fabric of the building other than those shown on the approved drawings. Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

MaterialsAll new external works and finishes, and any works of making good to the retained fabric, shall match the existing original work adjacent in respect of methods, detailed execution and finished appearance unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.
